scorecard.name: Empathy & Acknowledgment Statement
scorecard.coaching: At turn 1 and turn 20, the customer reported intense frustration and anxiety over severe telephone static preventing vital calls with her doctor, but you offered no empathetic validation.

scorecard.name: Paraphrasing
scorecard.coaching: You did not paraphrase or restate the customer's line noise issue in your own words at any point in the call.

scorecard.name: Active listening
scorecard.coaching: The customer stated her handset model at turn 7 (Panasonic cordless), but at turn 32 you asked her again what type of telephone handset she had.

grader.scenario: Landline crackling noise and static interference on master test socket
grader.notes: Martin demonstrates superb diagnostic methodology, running an exchange loop test and guiding Joanne to remove her NTE5 faceplate and isolate a corroded bell-wire on the test socket, restoring crystal-clear audio and doubling broadband speed. However, he shows three clear faults: he ignores Joanne's frustration, fails to paraphrase the problem, and repeats a question about the handset model.

items.name: Empathy & Acknowledgment Statement
items.evidence: [00:15] Customer: 'Our landline telephone has developed an unbearable crackling and hissing noise on the line. When anyone calls, there is so much static that you can barely hear a word...', Agent responds with verification questions without empathy.

items.name: Paraphrasing
items.evidence: Agent never restated the core issue in his own words; only confirmed email at turn 52.

items.name: Active listening
items.evidence: [01:10] Customer: 'We have a Panasonic cordless base station with two handsets.' followed by Agent at [06:30]: 'What type of telephone handset do you have there to plug in?'

items.name: Took ownership of the problem
items.evidence: [07:45] Agent stated: 'I will take direct ownership of this ticket and note that the internal bell-wire was safely isolated.'
